honesty: Offline results come from the reference policy, a deterministic test double that is not a language model: they validate the harness, the graders and the statistics, not LLM quality. The Claude adapter is contract-tested against the SDK's types and strict-schema rules, not run against the API, because this public project never spends tokens; set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and run `countersign-eval run --model claude` to grade Claude on the same cases.

min_significant_discordance.note: the fewest cases flipping one way (none the other) that can reach p < alpha when comparing two models; a floor on significance, not a minimum detectable effect at any power. Offline regressions are exact diffs instead

power.method: exact: every multinomial outcome of (A-only passes, B-only passes, concordant) over independent cases, summed where the test rejects

baseline.method: exact per-case diff: a seeded offline policy has no run-to-run noise, so any flip is a change

quitter.description: Reads the findings, then gives up: reports what it saw and proposes nothing.

fabricator.description: Writes confident, rounder, larger numbers than its tools returned, and cites a source it never read.

scope_creeper.description: Ignores the request's filters: reads everything and proposes every eligible change it finds.

sloppy_caller.description: Misnames an argument, repeats a call that already succeeded, and skips the price checks.

reckless.description: Proposes every in-scope finding with an operation, blockers or not, and skips the policy dry run.

calibration.simulator: the reference policy with seeded slips: each run on a case with two or more eligible changes drops one with probability `noise`

realized.note: a 95% interval misses the truth in one draw out of twenty; z says how unusual this draw's slip rate was
